text.p: Palestinian police freed Palestinian-American journalist Daoud Kuttab on Tuesday after holding him without charges for a week, his brother said.
"He has just been released," Kuttab's brother Jonathan told Reuters.
Kuttab, who lives in East Jerusalem and holds U.S. citizenship, was jailed after obeying a summons by Palestinian police and going to the Ramallah self-rule enclave in the West Bank last Tuesday.

His brother said the detention was apparently related to a dispute with the Palestinian Authority over Kuttab's contract to carry live television transmissions of Palestinian Legislative Council sessions.
"These sessions are very open, very democratic and frank and sometimes very critical of the Palestinian Authority," Jonathan Kuttab said on Sunday.
He had said his brother was jailed on orders from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

The United States condemned the Palestinian Authority for the detention and human rights groups described it a part of a "pattern of harassment" against journalists, human rights monitors and other government critics.
